image.subject: a heavy-set wealthy Puritan landowner in his forties, florid face, grey-streaked hair, a fine dark green wool coat with pewter buttons and a wide-brimmed black hat, Salem 1692, stepping through the door into the unheated Salem Village meetinghouse, bare timber walls, rows of plain wooden benches, breath visible in the cold, villagers on the benches turning to look at him as he enters

storyboard.claim: The adults learn the accusation game quickly; we move to Thomas Putnam in the meetinghouse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Putnam entering the cold meetinghouse as the crowded benches turn toward him: the powerful adult arriving on the stage where the panic is played out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sequence start (meetinghouse, Putnam): after Abigail, the camera turns to the adults.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces Putnam and the meetinghouse stage.

image.subject: inside the unheated Salem Village meetinghouse, bare timber walls, rows of plain wooden benches, breath visible in the cold, a packed congregation of Puritan villagers in grey and black wool, their breath pluming white in the freezing air, neighbours glancing suspiciously at each other across the benches

storyboard.claim: The crowded, freezing meetinghouse is thick with paranoia, a powder keg.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Breath clouds over a packed congregation where every face eyes a neighbour with suspicion: cold and distrust made visible.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same meetinghouse, wider: from Putnam to the whole suspicious crowd.
storyboard.addedInformation: The communal mood: freezing, crowded, suspicious.

image.subject: a heavy-set wealthy Puritan landowner in his forties, florid face, grey-streaked hair, a fine dark green wool coat with pewter buttons and a wide-brimmed black hat, Salem 1692, sitting on a meetinghouse bench whispering into the ear of the woman in black mourning, while his eyes look sideways past her through a small window toward wide green fields and a large prosperous farmstead on the far side

storyboard.claim: Putnam whispers to Ann about their seven dead babies while eyeing the Nurse family acres.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Putnam whispering to his grieving wife while his eyes slide away through the window to a rich farm: grief in his mouth, land in his eyes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same meetinghouse, close on the Putnams: the motive enters.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ann's loss and Thomas's real target, the Nurse land.

image.subject: wide sprawling fields of a prosperous 1692 Massachusetts farm, stone walls, a sturdy timber farmhouse and barns, a gentle white-haired Puritan grandmother in her seventies, lined kind face, grey wool dress, white shawl and white linen cap, Salem 1692 standing at the farmhouse gate, seen from far off as if watched from a distance

storyboard.claim: The coveted acres belong to the Nurse family; here the trials turn from religious panic into a legal mechanism.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Nurse farm seen from afar, Rebecca small at her gate: the land Putnam is staring at, the prize the court can deliver.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Result of 81: we see what Putnam's eyes were fixed on.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the Nurse property and Rebecca as its owner.

left.label: SPIRITUAL PURGE
left.subject: a gaunt middle-aged Puritan minister in a plain black coat and white preaching bands, thinning dark hair, anxious pinched face, Salem Village 1692, praying with eyes closed over an open Bible by candlelight

right.label: LAND GRAB
right.subject: a hand in a dark green wool cuff with pewter buttons sliding a folded parchment land deed and a stack of silver coins across a plank table by candlelight, Salem 1692

storyboard.claim: Accusations become the new currency: an economic incentive dressed as a spiritual purge.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Left a minister praying over a Bible, right a hand passing a land deed and coins across a table: what the purge claims to be vs. what it trades in.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalises the Putnam case into the rule.

image.subject: a heavy-set wealthy Puritan landowner in his forties, florid face, grey-streaked hair, a fine dark green wool coat with pewter buttons and a wide-brimmed black hat, Salem 1692, standing at the back of the unheated Salem Village meetinghouse, bare timber walls, rows of plain wooden benches, breath visible in the cold, glaring resentfully at an empty pulpit while a group of villagers walk out past him

storyboard.claim: Putnam nurses grievances: his brother-in-law was rejected as minister, largely by the Nurse faction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Putnam glaring at the empty pulpit as villagers file past: the post his family was refused.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to Putnam: the history behind his envy.

storyboard.claim: The Nurses started as renters, paid off 300 acres and rose by hard work, threatening Putnam's dominance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A single number carries it: 300 acres earned by former renters.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sequence (the land war, 85-90): the Nurses' rise.
storyboard.addedInformation: The size of the Nurse holding and how they got it.

stat.label: ACRES PAID OFF BY THE NURSES

image.subject: two groups of 1692 Puritan farmers facing each other angrily across a stone boundary wall at the edge of the woods, men gripping wooden staves and pulling at a broken fence rail, a heavy-set wealthy Puritan landowner in his forties, florid face, grey-streaked hair, a fine dark green wool coat with pewter buttons and a wide-brimmed black hat, Salem 1692, leading one side

storyboard.claim: The Nurses and Putnams even fought a two-day battle in the woods over boundaries; the court now offers a loophole to win it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two families squaring off over a stone boundary wall at the woods edge, Putnam leading one side: the property feud the court will settle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the land war: from status to open fight.

image.subject: a wiry, weathered farmer in his eighties, white stubble beard and bald crown, patched brown farm coat and breeches, Salem 1692, striding fast through the door into the Salem 1692 courtroom in the meetinghouse, judges at a raised bench in black robes, crowded benches, high rafters, waving a folded paper deposition over his head, heads on the benches turning toward him

storyboard.claim: Giles Corey, an old farmer who knows the law, charges into court with a deposition.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Giles barging into court brandishing his paper: the counter-attack arrives.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same land war, a new player challenges Putnam.

image.subject: a heavy-set wealthy Puritan landowner in his forties, florid face, grey-streaked hair, a fine dark green wool coat with pewter buttons and a wide-brimmed black hat, Salem 1692, bending down and whispering into the ear of a Puritan girl of about twelve in a white cap and grey dress, guiding her outstretched pointing arm toward a grey-bearded old man leaning on two walking sticks across a crowded courtroom

storyboard.claim: Giles says Putnam prompted his daughter to cry out on George Jacobs so Jacobs would hang and forfeit his land.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Putnam whispering into his daughter's ear and steering her pointing arm at old Jacobs: the prompted accusation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: What Giles's deposition alleges (cause).

storyboard.claim: A hanged witch's land is forfeit and auctioned, and only Putnam has the hard currency to buy it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A four-step chain: hanged -> land forfeit -> auction -> Putnam buys.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The legal mechanism behind 88's motive.
storyboard.addedInformation: Explains forfeiture and why Putnam alone benefits.

image.subject: a heavy-set wealthy Puritan landowner in his forties, florid face, grey-streaked hair, a fine dark green wool coat with pewter buttons and a wide-brimmed black hat, Salem 1692, standing alone on a cold hillside with his boot planted on a stone boundary marker, surveying neighbouring farms and fields spread out below him in grey morning light

storyboard.claim: It is a massive real estate grab, and he weaponises his wife's tragedy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Putnam with his boot on a boundary stone surveying other people's farms: the land grab as a posture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Result of the land-war sequence: Putnam the buyer.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sums the land motive before turning to Ann.

image.subject: a hollow-eyed Puritan woman in her late thirties in a black mourning dress and black hood, pale grief-worn face, Salem 1692, sobbing and clutching her hands to her chest in the Salem 1692 courtroom in the meetinghouse, judges at a raised bench in black robes, crowded benches, high rafters, while the heavy-set landowner in a green coat, stands calmly behind her with a hand on her shoulder, pushing her forward toward the judges

storyboard.claim: Thomas uses Ann's genuine hysteria as cover to destroy neighbours and take their land.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ann weeping in front while Thomas, calm behind her, pushes her toward the bench: her grief as his instrument.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sequence start (Ann vs Thomas, 91-99): the hosts' first reading.

storyboard.claim: Is Ann just a cover story? Calling it a pure real estate scheme feels too cynical.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A genuine question to the viewer: was Ann only a tool?
storyboard.onScreenText: WAS ANN JUST A COVER STORY?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Challenges 91.

image.subject: a frost-covered stone wall of a bleak Puritan churchyard at dusk, a black mourning hood and an unlit candle resting on it, bare trees beyond, Salem 1692

storyboard.claim: Ann's trauma is visceral: she laid seven unbaptised babies in the earth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ann kneeling by seven tiny graves: the loss counted out on the ground.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same Ann, now on her own terms: the cause of her grief.

image.subject: a hollow-eyed Puritan woman in her late thirties in a black mourning dress and black hood, pale grief-worn face, Salem 1692, sitting by a dying hearth at night staring fearfully into a dark corner of the room, an open Bible on her lap, a candle guttering beside her

storyboard.claim: In a world where the Devil walks the earth, such grief would make a mother believe in him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ann staring into the dark with a Bible on her lap: grief turning into fear of an unseen enemy.
storyboard.onScreenText: THE DEVIL WAS REAL TO HER
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Change: grief begins to look for a cause.

storyboard.claim: She needs an explanation, and Puritan theology offers one: witchcraft.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The word itself lands as the answer.
storyboard.onScreenText: SHE NEEDS AN EXPLANATION. THEOLOGY OFFERS ONE: WITCHCRAFT.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Result of 94: the explanation.

image.subject: a hollow-eyed Puritan woman in her late thirties in a black mourning dress and black hood, pale grief-worn face, Salem 1692, standing in the Salem 1692 courtroom in the meetinghouse, judges at a raised bench in black robes, crowded benches, high rafters, pointing a trembling accusing finger at the white-haired grandmother, who sits on a bench looking back at her in bewilderment

storyboard.claim: Ann truly believes Rebecca Nurse murdered her babies; her grief twists into paranoia.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ann's shaking finger aimed at gentle Rebecca: the grief has found its target.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Result of Ann's arc: belief becomes accusation.

image.subject: a heavy-set wealthy Puritan landowner in his forties, florid face, grey-streaked hair, a fine dark green wool coat with pewter buttons and a wide-brimmed black hat, Salem 1692, seated at a plank table signing a parchment complaint with a quill pen by candlelight, a magistrate's clerk standing beside him waiting to take it

storyboard.claim: Thomas directs the paranoia: he signs the first complaint against Rebecca and pushes Parris to declare witchcraft.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Putnam's own hand signing the complaint: the grief is Ann's, the paperwork is his.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turn: from Ann's belief to Thomas's action.
storyboard.addedInformation: Thomas as the legal author of the charge.

image.subject: a heavy-set wealthy Puritan landowner in his forties, florid face, grey-streaked hair, a fine dark green wool coat with pewter buttons and a wide-brimmed black hat, Salem 1692, looming over a gaunt middle-aged Puritan minister in a plain black coat and white preaching bands, thinning dark hair, anxious pinched face, Salem Village 1692, in a candlelit parsonage parlour, jabbing a finger at the minister's chest while Parris shrinks back against the wall

storyboard.claim: Putnam pushes Parris to declare witchcraft before Hale arrives and lends the children's cries his standing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Putnam towering over the cowering minister, finger at his chest: social standing used as force.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues 97: the second lever Putnam pulls.

image.subject: a heavy-set wealthy Puritan landowner in his forties, florid face, grey-streaked hair, a fine dark green wool coat with pewter buttons and a wide-brimmed black hat, Salem 1692, bent over a large hand-drawn parchment map of farm plots spread on a table by candlelight, measuring a neighbour's field with a pair of brass dividers, a quill and inkpot beside it

storyboard.claim: He turns private agony into public execution and calculates to the acre what a neighbour's reputation is worth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Putnam measuring a neighbour's plot with dividers on a land map: a reputation priced in acres.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Result of the Thomas sequence: the cold calculation.

storyboard.claim: The price of a name again; now to the moment the rules are codified.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The book's refrain as a typographic beat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the Putnam section; bridges to Tituba.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals the next scene: rules codified.

image.subject: a Black woman in her forties from Barbados, dark skin, a faded red headscarf, a coarse brown wool dress and shawl, Salem 1692, fallen to her knees on the floorboards of a candlelit parsonage parlour, hands raised in terror, as a gaunt middle-aged Puritan minister in a plain black coat and white preaching bands, thinning dark hair, anxious pinched face, Salem Village 1692, stands over her shouting, his face twisted with rage

storyboard.claim: In Parris's parlor Tituba falls to her knees in terror as Parris threatens to whip her to death.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tituba on her knees, hands raised, the minister screaming over her: the threat, never a blow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sequence start (the parlor interrogation, 101-116): one kept stage.

image.subject: a Black woman in her forties from Barbados, dark skin, a faded red headscarf, a coarse brown wool dress and shawl, Salem 1692, kneeling on the floor of a candlelit parsonage parlour, hemmed in by the gaunt Puritan minister in black, and the heavy-set landowner in a green coat, who leans down roaring at her

storyboard.claim: Putnam roars too; the pressure is suffocating, and here the court prints its price list.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same parlor, the circle closes: two men bearing down on the kneeling woman.
storyboard.onScreenText: THE COURT PRINTS ITS PRICE LIST
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage, pressure rises as Putnam joins.

left.label: DENY
left.subject: an empty noose rope hanging from the bare branch of an old oak on a rocky hill outside Salem against a grey dawn sky, 1692

right.label: CONFESS
right.subject: a Black woman in her forties from Barbados, dark skin, a faded red headscarf, a coarse brown wool dress and shawl, Salem 1692, kneeling with folded hands and bowed head in a candlelit parsonage parlour as a minister rests his hand on her head in blessing

storyboard.claim: If you deny the charge, as Tituba first does...
storyboard.concreteVisual: Left: denial = the empty noose; right: confession = the minister's blessing. The price list as two pictures.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same interrogation, the rule emerges.
storyboard.addedInformation: The two prices side by side.

image.subject: an empty noose rope hanging from the bare branch of an old oak on a rocky hill outside Salem at grey dawn in 1692, an oxcart on a dirt track and a crowd of townsfolk, no one beneath it

storyboard.claim: ...you face the rope. But if you confess...
storyboard.concreteVisual: The empty noose on the hill at dawn: the price of denial as a place and a symbol.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Result of 103's left side.

storyboard.claim: ...and crucially name others, you survive: a rigged plea bargain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The survival terms as a checklist.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the price list from 103-104.

image.subject: close view of a Black woman in her forties from Barbados, dark skin, a faded red headscarf, a coarse brown wool dress and shawl, Salem 1692, kneeling, glancing up warily at the stern faces of three Puritan men in black coats standing over her in a candlelit parlour, tears on her cheeks but her eyes sharp and calculating

storyboard.claim: Tituba realises denials are useless: the powerful men have decided she is guilty; they need a narrative.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tituba's wary upward look at the men: the moment she reads what they want.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same parlor: change inside Tituba, from denial to understanding.

image.subject: a Black woman in her forties from Barbados, dark skin, a faded red headscarf, a coarse brown wool dress and shawl, Salem 1692, kneeling and pointing wide-eyed toward a dark window as she speaks, while the young clergyman in black, leans in eagerly holding a heavy open leather book, a closed black leather-bound book on the table beside them

storyboard.claim: She says she saw the Devil and his book, but frames herself as a victim.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tituba describing the Devil to an eager Hale, the black book on the table: giving the theologians the story they want.
storyboard.onScreenText: SHE SAW THE DEVIL - AND HIS BOOK
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same parlor: her answer.

image.subject: a Black woman in her forties from Barbados, dark skin, a faded red headscarf, a coarse brown wool dress and shawl, Salem 1692, kneeling in a candlelit parsonage parlour, raising one arm to point toward the door, while the gaunt Puritan minister in black, and the heavy-set landowner in a green coat, lean forward eagerly to listen

storyboard.claim: Then she starts naming names, but not random names.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tituba's pointing arm and the men leaning in: names being handed over.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same parlor: confession becomes accusation.

image.subject: a ragged, homeless middle-aged woman in a torn dark shawl and soiled skirts, tangled grey hair, Salem 1692, begging at a farmhouse door, next to a dishevelled old woman slumped drunk against a fence with a clay jug, both shunned by passing Puritan villagers

storyboard.claim: She names Sarah Good and Goody Osburn, a beggar and a drunk, women Putnam had suggested.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The two outcasts at the village edge, shunned by passers-by: easy, powerless targets.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Result of the naming: who she picked.

image.subject: a striking young Puritan woman with long dark hair escaping a white linen cap, plain grey wool dress with a white collar and apron, intense dark eyes, Salem 1692, rising to her feet in a candlelit parsonage parlour with arms flung up toward the rafters and an ecstatic face, while a Black woman in her forties from Barbados, dark skin, a faded red headscarf, a coarse brown wool dress and shawl, Salem 1692, kneels beside her

storyboard.claim: The teenagers understand the economy at once: the second Tituba is saved, Abigail erupts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Abigail springing up in ecstasy beside the kneeling Tituba: seizing the same exit.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same parlor, new actor copying Tituba.

storyboard.claim: "I saw Goody Booth! I saw Goody Hawkins!" - an ecstatic chorus of names.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The names stacked like a chant.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues 110: what she cries.

image.subject: a scholarly Puritan clergyman in his late thirties, clean-shaven earnest face, black clerical coat and white bands, carrying a stack of heavy leather books, Massachusetts 1692, kneeling beside a Black woman in her forties from Barbados, dark skin, a faded red headscarf, a coarse brown wool dress and shawl, Salem 1692, and praying over her with one hand gently on her shoulder, Tituba weeping with her face in her hands, candlelight

storyboard.claim: Tituba is terrified and weeping as Hale prays over her, giving her a strange spiritual respect, almost for the first time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hale kneeling to pray with his hand on her shoulder: the minister treating her as a soul.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same parlor, back to Tituba after Abigail.

storyboard.claim: Did she break mentally under the threat of death and truly believe she was doing God's work?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A real open question.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Raises a counter-reading of 112.

image.subject: a Black woman in her forties from Barbados, dark skin, a faded red headscarf, a coarse brown wool dress and shawl, Salem 1692, kneeling with a tear-streaked face in a candlelit parlour, eyes lowered but glancing sideways, watching the men's reactions closely as she speaks

storyboard.claim: The terror is real, but her choice of targets reveals a calculation that survives the panic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tears on her face but eyes watching the men's reactions: fear and calculation in one frame.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers 113: both are true.

left.label: SPARED
left.subject: a heavy-set wealthy Puritan landowner in his forties, florid face, grey-streaked hair, a fine dark green wool coat with pewter buttons and a wide-brimmed black hat, Salem 1692, standing confidently with arms folded in a candlelit parlour

right.label: NAMED
right.subject: a ragged, homeless middle-aged woman in a torn dark shawl and soiled skirts, tangled grey hair, Salem 1692, being led away by the arm by a constable down a muddy village lane

storyboard.claim: She does not accuse the powerful; she feeds them the outcasts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Left the spared powerful (Putnam), right the named outcast (Sarah Good) led away.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Develops 114: the pattern in her targets.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts who is safe and who is sacrificed.

image.subject: a Black woman in her forties from Barbados, dark skin, a faded red headscarf, a coarse brown wool dress and shawl, Salem 1692, standing free at the parsonage doorway in morning light, watching a ragged, homeless middle-aged woman in a torn dark shawl and soiled skirts, tangled grey hair, Salem 1692, being led away down the muddy lane by a constable toward the jail

storyboard.claim: Pure calculated survival: she trades others' lives to keep her own breath, setting the town's exchange rate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tituba free at the door while Sarah Good is led to jail: one life traded for another.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Result of the Tituba sequence: the trade completed.

image.subject: a thin, officious court clerk in his forties in a dark brown coat, a black hat and a leather satchel of papers, Salem 1692, walking up a muddy spring lane toward a lone farmhouse at dusk, a folded arrest warrant in his hand, young green leaves on the trees

storyboard.claim: Tituba proves the price of a name; the exchange rate evolves into premeditated assassinations. Fast forward to spring.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cheever walking toward a farmhouse with a warrant in spring: the next targeting is on its way.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Bridge to the Proctor farmhouse scene (118).
storyboard.addedInformation: Time jump and the coming warrant.
